source_snapshot.procedure: Enter BIOS -> Advanced -> Core Watchdog and check information; generic setup/evidence steps request log clearing.
source_snapshot.criteria: All information should match SPEC definition.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL with ipmitool, while explicitly stating stock ipmitool has no direct high-level Core Watchdog command and supplying no evidence output.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: MANUAL ONLY; the essential evidence is the read-only BIOS page, with exact watchdog status/timeout/action/OEM semantics and no guessed raw command.

historical_reviews.deepseek: Its limitation is valid, but PARTIAL is not supported because the row provides no automatable command or non-UI acceptance checkpoint.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: The classification is changed to MANUAL ONLY and the watchdog oracle is made explicit; optional OS/BMC data remains supporting only.
historical_reviews.history: Exact-code searches found no duplicate variant or earlier completed record; other watchdog tests cannot supply this row's BIOS field mapping.
historical_reviews.v3_1: BIOS core-watchdog fields may represent enable state, timeout, action or OEM policy and are not equivalent to generic BMC watchdog state exposed by stock ipmitool.

original_test_intent: Have a qualified operator inspect every BIOS Advanced Core Watchdog field and verify its displayed state or parameter against the owner-approved platform specification without changing or arming the watchdog.
original_method: Bind the exact SUT, CPU, BIOS and AGESA; enumerate the Core Watchdog labels and enabled/timeout/action/OEM meanings; traverse the BIOS page read-only, capture each value and compare with the approved matrix; preserve watchdog/boot logs and exit unchanged.
manual_activity: A qualified operator captures each Core Watchdog BIOS label/value and compares enabled state, timeout and action semantics with the approved firmware-specific matrix while ensuring the watchdog is neither changed nor triggered.
required_inputs: Exact SUT, CPU, BIOS and AGESA identity
OEM units, encoding and optional-field semantics
Optional exact read-only OEM interface only if independently documented
safety_requirements: Do not enable, disable, re-arm or change timeout/action
Do not run a guessed ipmitool raw request
Do not infer BIOS Core Watchdog state from a generic BMC watchdog command
Do not clear dmesg, syslog or SEL
Stop on reset, countdown, unexpected state change, boot warning or OEM ambiguity
agent_execution_scope: Prepare the watchdog field/OEM comparison matrix
Support read-only SUT and boot-health collection
Coordinate but do not claim BIOS UI control
Accept an OEM readback only when command and decoder are owner-approved
engineer_actions: Approve field meanings, units, timeout and action oracle
Determine whether any OEM readback is equivalent
Resolve unexpected watchdog state and own PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: DeepSeek correctly says stock ipmitool cannot run the BIOS check, so its PARTIAL label has no executable component in this row.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Manual operator: verify platform identity, enter Advanced -> Core Watchdog, capture every displayed field and compare it with the approved OEM matrix without changing settings or triggering recovery.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Core Watchdog information check and 20/20-minute estimates remain; ipmitool is not treated as a substitute and logs are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.status: MANUAL READ-ONLY CORE WATCHDOG FIELD AUDIT
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a matrix of BIOS label, expected enable state, timeout value/units, recovery action, OEM semantics, observed value and protected evidence.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Removes unsupported partial automation and prevents a generic or raw ipmitool command from being treated as authoritative BIOS evidence.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Optional OS/BMC watchdog data can show related runtime state but does not cover the BIOS page unless the owner proves exact field equivalence.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Watchdog namespaces may be independent; misidentifying one can hide an armed reset source or incorrectly qualify recovery policy.

project_override_considerations: A Project may provide an exact OEM read-only command and decoder, but it must map each response field to the BIOS page before it can supplement the operator capture. Mutation or timeout-expiry testing is separate approval-gated work.
expected_evidence: Protected capture of every BIOS Core Watchdog field
Any optional owner-approved read-only cross-check with command/decoder provenance
Preserved watchdog/boot/event evidence and no-trigger/no-mutation confirmation
Engineer-owned PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Test Set, Procedure and Criteria consistently specify BIOS Core Watchdog information inspection. DeepSeek's unsupported PARTIAL/ipmitool suggestion is a prior-review limitation, not a conflict in the Master row.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The manual inspection is safely defined once the owner supplies the firmware-specific field/OEM matrix and a qualified operator can capture the page.

review_improvement: Changes unsupported PARTIAL automation to MANUAL ONLY and binds each watchdog state, timeout and action to firmware-specific semantics without arming or triggering it.
independent_technical_reasoning: A platform can expose distinct CPU core, firmware, OS and BMC watchdogs. An ipmitool response for one watchdog does not prove the BIOS Core Watchdog control, so equivalence must be documented rather than inferred and the UI remains the authoritative evidence for this row.
